Yes. On 16 June the plant exceeded the 1250 kW contract limit:

- Peak: **1324.4 kW** at 08:15, which is 1.06× the contract [data: get_demand]
- Two intervals over contract: 08:00 (1307.1 kW) and 08:15 (1324.4 kW) [data: get_demand]

This is the Monday-morning simultaneous-start scenario (S2): demand jumped from ~540 kW at 07:45 to ~1307 kW at 08:00 as the SMT lines and ovens started together. It recovered to ~1080 kW by 09:00 and stayed below contract for the rest of the day.

According to the documents:

**Why OFF, not standby:** A reflow oven in standby draws 36% of its 70 kW rating = 25.2 kW continuously for as long as it stays on, while producing nothing. A switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]. Standby is a large idle load, so ovens must be switched fully off after the line stops (and only when no boards are inside) [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-01_reflow_oven.md#EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual > Energy-saving notes].

**Excess energy in S5:** RF-02 was left in standby from 2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20. Weekend energy was about 1,556 kWh versus about 346 kWh normal — an excess of about 1,210 kWh from that single oven [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

Note: the documents give the energy figure but not a dollar cost. I can convert it to NT$ using the tariff if you want — just say the word.

answer:
According to SOP-03 Step 2 (the playbook shed order), the first load shed is **EV-01 charging** (pause 100% of EV-01).

Loads that must never be shed: the **server room, running molders mid-cycle, and reflow ovens with boards inside** [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order].

The full shed order is: (1) pause EV charging (EV-01), (2) delay next burn-in loading (BI-01, BI-02), (3) raise chilled-water setpoint +1°C (CH-01, CH-02), (4) lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar (AC-01–AC-03) [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order].
